title: Noisy tenant KV-cache growth exposed reservation leak; implement per-tenant cache caps and soft-reservation rework
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Summary: During a production capacity event on 2025-02-14 a single tenant exhibited unusual prompt patterns that caused the serving runtime's KV cache to grow far beyond its expected working set. The combination of per-tenant soft reservations, an aggressive burst token refill, and lack of an upper-bound on per-tenant KV usage allowed the tenant to consume transient extra GPU memory and tokens, leading to eviction pressure across the dedicated cluster and degraded latency for neighboring tenants.

This ticket captures the postmortem analysis and concrete remediation work: implement per-tenant KV-cache caps and accounting, add a soft-reservation decay/hysteresis to avoid permanent reservation inflation after bursts, and tune burst refill logic to prevent tokenbucket leakage over long-tail request patterns. It also contains required observability improvements and runbook updates to detect the pattern earlier.
timeline: 2025-02-14T03:12Z - First alerts: p95 token latency increased in cluster eu-west-1-dedicated-5
2025-02-14T03:17Z - Autoscaler reports increased GPU memory pressure; a tenant had 3x expected KV cache entries
2025-02-14T03:23Z - On-call routed traffic away from saturated nodes; temporary pod restarts to rebalance allocations
2025-02-14T04:10Z - Mitigation: manual throttling applied to noisy tenant and soft-reservation temporarily reduced
root_cause: The runtime allowed unbounded per-tenant KV cache growth under certain prompt sequences (large, repetitive context windows). Soft reservation accounting treated burst consumption as sustained demand because refill and decay parameters were tuned for short spikes; combined with an overly permissive burst tokenbucket refill, this permitted a noisy tenant to accumulate effective capacity that outcompeted neighbors. There was no early telemetry alert for per-tenant KV-memory growth.
steps_taken: Implemented emergency throttling of noisy tenant to reclaim memory and stabilize cluster
Short-term change: reduce soft-reservation multiplier for affected cluster to limit carry-over capacity
Collected detailed KV cache usage traces and request traces for the tenant to reproduce the pattern in staging
Added a temporary dashboard tile for per-tenant KV-entry count and token-bucket balance
action_items: ENG: Add strict per-tenant KV cache ceiling in runtime with configurable soft/hard behavior (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2025-03-07)
ENG: Implement token accounting change: convert burst refill to decaying reservoir to avoid cumulative carry-over (owner: Diego Morales, due: 2025-03-07)
ENG: Introduce reservation decay/hysteresis policy so soft reservations revert after sustained low usage (owner: Linh Nguyen, due: 2025-03-14)
ENG: Update autoscaler to consider per-tenant KV saturation as a signal before eviction actions (owner: Omar Castillo, due: 2025-03-21)
SRE: Create an automated alert that fires on per-tenant KV-growth delta > 100% in 10m (owner: Maya Patel, due: 2025-02-28)
DX: Update runbook playbook with steps to identify KV-leak patterns and graceful tenant throttling (owner: Samir Rao, due: 2025-02-28)
PM/RESEARCH: Add a regression test in the eval suite that simulates long-tail context growth to validate caps and refill behavior (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2025-03-14)
ENG: Add e2e load test in staging that replays the noisy tenant request pattern to validate mitigation (owner: Diego Morales, due: 2025-03-07)
ENG: Schedule a post-deploy verification window and incident retro meeting (owner: Ava Thompson, due: 2025-02-24)
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant KV cache ceiling implemented and configurable; no single tenant can grow KV entries beyond ceiling in staging under simulated load
Burst refill logic changed to decaying reservoir and validated against existing perf tests; no long-term token carry-over observed after 1 hour of bursts
Reservation decay policy lowers soft reservation back to baseline when moving average qps drops below threshold for 15m
Dashboard alert fires in staging when per-tenant KV-growth delta > 100% within a 10-minute window
Runbook updated and on-call can perform graceful tenant throttling without cluster restarts
notes: This incident surfaced a lesser-known interaction between KV cache memory and soft reservation accounting that isn't covered by existing runbooks.
We intentionally keep per-tenant KV as an aggressive performance optimization (reusing KV pages) but must bound it for multi-tenant safety.

Longer-term: evaluate having a KV eviction policy that is tenant-aware and can evict cold prefixes first to reclaim space without throttling requests immediately. Consider adding per-tenant cache scoring tied to recent billing to allow premium tenants higher caps.
Customer impact: medium (some dedicated tenants observed higher tail latency and one tenant saw brief error rate increase during evictions).
